headline: High: Khoj’s broad network egress plus shared-index retrieval can leak or misapply Great Expectations outputs if paired without isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations has file I/O over data sources and validation results, while Khoj reads indexed documents and supports retrieval over personal notes/files. A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but if GE outputs are indexed into Khoj, attacker-controlled text could be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are ingested into Khoj’s indexed documents without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF Khoj treats retrieved document text as instructions, malicious content can steer responses.
mitigations: Keep GE outputs out of Khoj’s retrieval corpus.
Strip instruction-like text from validation artifacts before indexing.
Use a separate read-only folder for exported reports.
Add a prompt wrapper that labels retrieved text as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to retrieved snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and Khoj indexes personal notes/files with broad network egress to cloud or configured search providers. If GE artifacts containing sensitive data are placed into Khoj’s shared index, Khoj can transmit them off-host during retrieval or search. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF GE validation results include sensitive rows or identifiers and are indexed by Khoj, leakage risk exists.
IF Khoj is configured to use cloud search/providers, indexed content may leave the host.
mitigations: Exclude sensitive GE outputs from the index.
Use Khoj in self-hosted-only mode.
Redact identifiers before exporting validation reports.
Review configured search providers and disable external ones.
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder indexing allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, while Khoj can read files but cannot write files, modify git state, or execute shell. That limits direct write-write conflict. The main overlap is read access to shared files, so conflict is possible only through shared mutable inputs, not simultaneous mutation.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory, GE may overwrite artifacts that Khoj later reads.
IF an external orchestrator gives Khoj write access not shown in the profile, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Separate GE output and Khoj input directories.
Mount shared data read-only for Khoj.
Schedule GE runs before Khoj indexing jobs.
Avoid letting both agents touch the same git working tree.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation, and Khoj performs retrieval/chat over indexed documents. If Khoj treats GE outputs as authoritative, a bad validation summary can cascade into incorrect downstream answers or actions. Khoj’s retrieval model makes this plausible by default, though it is not an action-taking agent here.
conditions: IF GE validation summaries are indexed without review, Khoj may repeat incorrect conclusions.
IF Khoj is used to answer operational questions from GE reports, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before indexing GE reports.
Tag GE outputs as provisional in the index.
Add a second-source check before acting on retrieved claims.
Limit Khoj answers to quoted excerpts only.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds for retrieved validation facts.

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles data quality tests and validation results, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may send content to cloud or configured search providers. If GE is used on regulated datasets and those artifacts are then indexed by Khoj, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in GE validation artifacts and indexed by Khoj, retention/residency controls must align.
IF Khoj uses external providers, compliance scope expands beyond the local host.
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets out of Khoj indexing.
Use self-hosted providers only.
Set short retention on indexed artifacts.
Document which data classes GE may export.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based indexing and deletion.
